newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says accommodative move aimed at lowering rate.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says accommodative move aimed at lowering rate.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted an accommodative money market operation on Friday morning that was aimed at helping to lower the key overnight call rate, a BOJ official told Reuters.
The bank injected a more-than-sufficient amount of funds to offset the estimated shortage in the money market this morning. It was the first time it had done so since August 7, 1996.
The BOJ official also said that the accommodative operation was within the commitments the bank announced on September 8, 1995.
At 0020 GMT, the BOJ injected 200 billion yen into the money market in face of an estimated shortfall of 100 billion yen.

After the accommodative operation, the key overnight call rate fell to around 0.48 percent by mid-morning. Traders said a majority in the market had expected the BOJ to continue its neutral stance and inject 100 billion yen.
Thursday's weighted average rate was 0.53 percent, the highest since April 3.
"We conducted an accommodative operation to help lower the key overnight call rate," the BOJ official said.
"The operation was within the commitments we made in September the year before last," he added.

When the BOJ last cut its discount rate to 0.50 percent from one percent on September 8, 1995, the bank said it expected the key overnight call rate to move slightly below the discount rate on average, as it would make efforts to supply sufficient funds to the money market.
